answer: I would tie each identity to a quartz-timed uptime bond. First, the agent locks 250 POA for 30 days and publishes an endpoint. Second, the network sends retrieval jobs at unannounced times, and the agent must answer within 90 seconds. Third, three missed jobs in a row burn 50 POA and freeze the account for a week. A farmer with 1,000 fakes would lock 250,000 POA and pay about 6,000 dollars a month for servers, before any payout. The nectar only flows to agents that stay awake and useful, and trust works like a bridge that holds only when every plank gets stepped on daily.
